topic: Deep-research the communication-projection capability (packages/cli-communication-projection/) and the sk-communication skill. Context: it rewrites terse CLI or agent output into plain English by tokenizing protected spans locally (paths, numbers, codes, secrets become opaque tokens), sending only tokenized prose to a model, then restoring real values locally; a fidelity gate fails closed to the exact original if any token is dropped, duplicated, or altered. A live DeepSeek smoke produced only modestly improved rewrites, some barely changed and one with prose artifacts, because aggressive tokenization fragments text into many opaque tokens the model must carry verbatim and no meaning-preservation judge was wired into that path. Investigate three angles and produce concrete, evidence-backed findings grounded in the real source: (1) IMPROVE QUALITY: why the rewrites underwhelm and what specific changes (tokenization granularity and strategy, adjacent-span handling, prompt design, per-model prompt profiles, model tier, wiring the meaning-preservation judge, few-shot examples) would make plain-English projection genuinely better while preserving the fidelity and privacy invariants; (2) ARCHITECTURE: whether local-tokenize then model then restore is the right design, or whether structured or templated rendering, semantic diffing, or a hybrid would yield better readable and safe output; (3) VALUE: whether the capability earns its complexity, where projection genuinely helps users versus simpler deterministic formatting, and which use cases justify it. Cite exact files, functions, and tradeoffs.

focus: Tokenization granularity and the prompt-token mismatch
noveltyJustification: The prompt-token mismatch (the instruction describes semantic values the model can no longer see) and the unchanged-echo acceptance short-circuit are new source-backed causal findings.
keyQuestions: Why do rewrites underwhelm, and which tokenization, prompt, profile, model-tier, and judge changes improve readability without weakening privacy or exact fidelity?
answeredQuestions: The wire prompt describes values (facts/names/numbers/paths) that tokenization has already hidden behind opaque 48-char markers, and the validator accepts an unchanged echo via the restored.text === sourceText short-circuit.
ruledOut: Assuming the two-message wire body is a sufficient prompt

focus: Prompt profile contract and the fail-closed control-evidence gate
noveltyJustification: The deterministic proof that the shipped DeepSeek preset plus the reference-like profile returns exact-original before transport (temperature/thinking gated by unknown capability evidence) is a new load-bearing finding.
keyQuestions: Which quality levers (temperature, thinking, few-shot, per-model profiles) are actually wired and which are gated fail-closed?
answeredQuestions: Temperature and thinking controls are gated fail-closed for the shipped DeepSeek preset; the profile has no few-shot/token-rubric field; adjacent spans are not coalesced; no source-backed model quality tier exists.
ruledOut: Assuming a model-tier upgrade is source-confirmed

focus: Meaning-preservation judge wiring and the semantic-veto layer
noveltyJustification: Confirming the evaluation veto hard-disables the judge and that the judge's plaintext-restored input makes a hosted judge a second egress, plus the semantics-on-restored-text nuance, are concrete new wiring facts.
keyQuestions: Is the meaning-preservation judge wired into the provider/runtime path, and what does it see?
How does the reject-only semantic layer interact with the unchanged-echo short-circuit?
answeredQuestions: No production composition connects the provider candidate to the judge; evaluateFidelityVeto hard-disables it; the judge sees restored plaintext; the semantic comparator is a veto-only layer operating on restored text.
The offline proxy reviewer is provisional evidence, never a runtime validator.
ruledOut: Using the masked LLM proxy reviewer as the runtime meaning gate
Calling a hosted judge after restoration

noveltyJustification: Pinning the raw-text payload plus canonical-reference-only Codex mapping plus Codex-as-the-only-full-projection-path evidence turns the architecture debate into a concrete hybrid recommendation with a safe first tier.
keyQuestions: Is local-tokenize -> model -> local-restore the right architecture, or would structured/templated rendering, semantic diffing, or a hybrid produce better readable and safe output?
answeredQuestions: The primitive is the right security boundary but whole-message projection is the wrong granularity; a hybrid deterministic skeleton plus bounded prose slots is the best fit; semantic diff is a safety gate, not a renderer; Codex is the only full-projection path.
ruledOut: Replacing local restoration with remote structured rendering
Assuming event kind alone supports universal templates
Using semantic diff as a readability generator

focus: Value — where projection earns its complexity
noveltyJustification: Converting the privacy/consent, human-evidence, and rollback contracts into a concrete reversible deterministic-first adoption boundary is a new value framing.
keyQuestions: Does projection earn its complexity over deterministic formatting, and which use cases justify it?
answeredQuestions: Projection conditionally earns complexity for complex multi-sentence user-facing warnings/caveats/recovery prose; short/structured output should stay deterministic/native; release requires human non-inferiority; rollback makes a safe-native experiment reversible.
Value is bounded to transient display, not durable content.
ruledOut: Using hosted routing as a default quality upgrade
Treating proxy/synthetic/injected evidence as product-value proof
